title: Code of Conduct and Ethics (containing the Employee Share Trading Policy, paragraphs 3.39 to 3.49)
date_approved: Changes require approval from the Policy Owner (Company Secretary) and the Executive Sponsor (General Counsel); the restrictions on Nominated Qantas Employees were endorsed by the Qantas Board. No approval date stated.
date_next_review: Reviewed by the Policy Owner at a minimum annually; no date stated

tiers.name: Qantas Employees
tiers.description: Directors, employees, contractors and agents of the Qantas Group and any person or organisation that acts for it. Subject only to the legal insider trading prohibition (paragraphs 3.41 to 3.43): no closed periods, no clearance requirement and no hedging, margin lending or encumbrance restriction applies to this tier.

tiers.name: Nominated Qantas Employees
tiers.description: Directors, Company Secretaries, Executive Management Members (direct reports to the CEO), direct reports to Executive Management Members, and other Executives specifically notified by the CEO or his nominee from time to time. Treated as routinely in possession of Material Non-Public Information and subject to the Closed Periods, the written Request to Deal regime and the extended Dealing definition in paragraph 3.45.

tiers.name: family member or associate over whom they have influence
tiers.description: Any family member or associate over whom a Nominated Qantas Employee has influence, including specifically any person who lives in the same home as the Nominated Qantas Employee. The paragraph 3.44 prohibition applies to them directly.

definitions.hedging_definition: hedging or otherwise entering into a contract with the purpose of securing a profit or avoiding a loss by reference to fluctuations in the price of the Securities of Qantas or any Qantas Group listed entity

applies_to: family member or associate over whom they have influence
windows.start_anchor: 31 December (end of the financial period ending 31 December)
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after the release to the ASX of the half-year financial results for that period

applies_to: family member or associate over whom they have influence
windows.start_anchor: 30 June (end of the financial period ending 30 June)
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after the release to the ASX of the full-year financial results for that period

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: No power to impose additional or ad hoc blackout periods is conferred by the Code. The only discretionary extension of the restricted population is the CEO's (or his nominee's) power to notify further Executives that they are Nominated Qantas Employees, which brings them within the standing Closed Periods and approval regime.

rules.detail: The Securities definition expressly reaches derivatives 'issued or created over the listed entity's securities by third parties', with no venue limit, so a bank-written OTC put or call over Qantas shares is a Security. Paragraph 3.45(a) then extends Dealing for Nominated Qantas Employees to prohibit any contract entered into with the purpose of securing a profit or avoiding a loss by reference to price fluctuations, which is exactly what the two collar legs do. The paragraph is not limited by vesting state.
rules.evidence: For Nominated Qantas Employees, the definition of Dealing is further extended to prohibit: hedging or otherwise entering into a contract with the purpose of securing a profit or avoiding a loss by reference to fluctuations in the price of the Securities of Qantas or any Qantas Group listed entity

rules.detail: Paragraph 3.45 applies only to Nominated Qantas Employees, and the Closed Period and approval regime in 3.44 is expressly confined to them. An ordinary Qantas Employee is subject only to the statutory insider trading prohibition, so a derivative over Qantas Securities is permitted provided the employee holds no Material Non-Public Information.
rules.evidence: Qantas Employees must not Deal in Qantas Securities while in possession of Material Non-Public Information.

rules.detail: Purpose-based hedging ban with no vesting carve-out and no venue limit. On the alternative reading that 3.45 merely enlarges the Dealing definition so that hedging falls within the 3.44 regime, a hedge over vested shares would instead require a written Request to Deal approved by the Chairman, Board, CEO or Company Secretary and would be barred in Closed Periods.
rules.evidence: hedging or otherwise entering into a contract with the purpose of securing a profit or avoiding a loss by reference to fluctuations in the price of the Securities of Qantas or any Qantas Group listed entity

rules.detail: Absolute for unvested holdings. Restricted Securities under a Qantas employee share plan may vest and transfer automatically, but the exception does not permit any other Dealing in them, and the exceptional-circumstances clearance in 3.48 is expressly unavailable for unvested Securities.
rules.evidence: Under exceptional circumstances, a Nominated Qantas Employee, who is not in possession of Material Non-Public Information in relation to Qantas or any Qantas Group listed entity, may be given clearance to Deal as outlined in paragraphs 3.44 and 3.46, except in relation to Securities that are unvested.

rules.detail: Restricted Securities that have vested but remain subject to plan restrictions cannot be otherwise Dealt with; the automatic removal of restrictions or transfer is the only permitted event.
rules.evidence: the automatic removal of restrictions or transfer to a Nominated Qantas Employee of Qantas Securities pursuant to the terms of a Qantas employee share plan established by the Qantas Board (Restricted Securities). However, this paragraph does not permit the Nominated Qantas Employee to otherwise Deal in those Restricted Securities

rules.detail: The hedging extension in 3.45 is expressly limited to Nominated Qantas Employees; the Code says nothing about hedging by other employees.

Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward, share swap or structured note is a Security ('any structured financial product, swap, futures contract') and, if entered into to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to the Qantas share price, is caught by the 3.45(a) purpose test. A monetisation secured on the shares is separately caught by 3.45(b).
rules.evidence: means shares, options or other securities or derivatives (including any structured financial product, swap, futures contract, contract for difference, spread bet, warrant or depository receipt) issued by any listed entity or issued or created over the listed entity's securities by third parties.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the Code. For Nominated Qantas Employees a short position taken to profit from a price fall would in substance be a contract entered into to secure a profit by reference to price fluctuations under 3.45(a), but the Code does not say so.
Securities lending arrangements are named in the same limb as margin lending and encumbrance, qualified by the same 'where control of any sale process relating to those Securities may be lost' test.
rules.evidence: any margin lending or securities lending arrangement, or otherwise granting a charge, lien or other encumbrance ... over the Securities of Qantas or any Qantas Group listed entity, where control of any sale process relating to those Securities may be lost.

rules.detail: Contracts for difference and spread bets are expressly named in the Securities definition, so dealing in one is a Dealing; for Nominated Qantas Employees a CFD entered into to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to the Qantas price is also caught by the 3.45(a) hedging limb.
rules.evidence: other securities or derivatives (including any structured financial product, swap, futures contract, contract for difference, spread bet, warrant or depository receipt)

rules.detail: Margin lending arrangements over Qantas Securities are prohibited for Nominated Qantas Employees where control of any sale process may be lost. The qualifier is the operative test: a facility under which the lender can sell the shares without the borrower's direction is caught.
rules.evidence: any margin lending or securities lending arrangement, or otherwise granting a charge, lien or other encumbrance (including a mortgage, charge, pledge, lien or title retention arrangement, right of set off or right to withhold payment of a deposit or other money, or any third party interest such as a trust or an equity) over the Securities of Qantas or any Qantas Group listed entity, where control of any sale process relating to those Securities may be lost.

rules.detail: An unusually wide encumbrance list: mortgage, charge, pledge, lien, title retention, right of set off, right to withhold payment of a deposit or other money, and any third party interest such as a trust or an equity. All are prohibited where control of any sale process over the Securities may be lost.
rules.evidence: otherwise granting a charge, lien or other encumbrance (including a mortgage, charge, pledge, lien or title retention arrangement, right of set off or right to withhold payment of a deposit or other money, or any third party interest such as a trust or an equity) over the Securities of Qantas or any Qantas Group listed entity, where control of any sale process relating to those Securities may be lost.

rules.detail: Paragraph 3.45(b) is confined to Nominated Qantas Employees; the Code is silent on encumbrances granted by other employees.

Not limited to margin loans: any grant of security over Qantas Securities for any financing is prohibited if control of the sale process may be lost, and the list extends to rights of set off and rights to withhold payment, which are standard features of a bank's security package for a funded collar.
rules.evidence: any margin lending or securities lending arrangement, or otherwise granting a charge, lien or other encumbrance ... where control of any sale process relating to those Securities may be lost.

rules.detail: The Code imposes no holding period, buy-sell window, intention test or instrument maturity test. Nothing prevents a short-dated instrument on tenor grounds.

clearance.approver: Chairman, Board (in the case of the Chairman), CEO or the Company Secretary (as appropriate); exceptional-circumstances clearance only from the Chairman or CEO
clearance.evidence: outside the Closed Periods, without providing the Chairman, Board (in the case of the Chairman), CEO or the Company Secretary (as appropriate) with a written Request to Deal in Qantas Securities and receiving written approval permitting them to undertake the requested Dealing.

Nominated Qantas Employees are routinely in possession of Material Non-Public Information. Therefore, Nominated Qantas Employees (or any family member or associate over whom they have influence, including specifically any person who lives in the same home as the Nominated Qantas Employee) are prohibited from Dealing in the Securities of Qantas or any Qantas Group listed entity

exceptions.evidence: the automatic removal of restrictions or transfer to a Nominated Qantas Employee of Qantas Securities pursuant to the terms of a Qantas employee share plan established by the Qantas Board (Restricted Securities). However, this paragraph does not permit the Nominated Qantas Employee to otherwise Deal in those Restricted Securities

ongoing participation in a dividend reinvestment plan or an employee share purchase plan. However, electing to participate (or amend participation) in such a plan remains subject to the prohibition in paragraph 3.44

exceptions.approver: Qantas Board (approval of the plan determining the timing and structure of the offer)
exceptions.evidence: Dealing under an offer or invitation made to all or most Qantas shareholders, such as a rights issue, security purchase plan, or equal access buy-back where the plan that determines the timing and structure of the offer has been approved by the Qantas Board
trading under a non-discretionary trading plan in accordance with the Qantas Employee Share Trading Procedure.

exceptions.approver: Chairman or CEO, in writing (including via electronic means)
exceptions.evidence: For the purposes of this paragraph “exceptional circumstances” includes: severe financial hardship; court orders requiring the sale of the securities; a legal or regulatory requirement; or other circumstances deemed exceptional by the CEO or Chairman.
court orders requiring the sale of the securities

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No price-trigger guidance, but the operative test is loss of control of the sale process: paragraph 3.45(b) prohibits margin lending, securities lending and any charge, lien, encumbrance, right of set off or third party interest over Qantas Securities 'where control of any sale process relating to those Securities may be lost'. A facility under which the lender cannot sell without the borrower's direction is outside the prohibition on its face.

external_documents: Qantas Employee Share Trading Procedure (governs the Request to Deal process and non-discretionary trading plans)
Retention and Storage of Records Procedure
exemption_authority: Chairman or CEO only, in writing (including electronically), under paragraph 3.48, for a Nominated Qantas Employee not in possession of Material Non-Public Information, in exceptional circumstances (severe financial hardship, court orders requiring the sale of the securities, a legal or regulatory requirement, or other circumstances deemed exceptional by the CEO or Chairman). The approval is valid for one month unless another period is agreed, and cannot be granted in relation to unvested Securities. On its terms it releases the paragraph 3.44 prohibition only, so it is unclear whether it can authorise a paragraph 3.45 hedge or encumbrance.
jurisdiction_overlays: Corporations Act section 1043A (Australian insider trading prohibition)
the laws of other countries in which the Qantas Group operates that prohibit dealing while in possession of Material Non-Public Information
ASX Listing Rules (continuous disclosure and Listing Rule 12.10)

bespoke_clauses.clause: For Nominated Qantas Employees, the definition of Dealing is further extended to prohibit: (a) hedging or otherwise entering into a contract with the purpose of securing a profit or avoiding a loss by reference to fluctuations in the price of the Securities of Qantas ...; and (b) any margin lending or securities lending arrangement, or otherwise granting a charge, lien or other encumbrance ... where control of any sale process relating to those Securities may be lost.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This single paragraph blocks both legs of a funded collar for directors and executives, and its drafting is ambiguous between a flat ban and an enlargement of Dealing that would leave both legs available with a written Request to Deal outside Closed Periods; the point should be settled with the Company Secretary before any structuring work.

bespoke_clauses.topic: loss of control of sale process
bespoke_clauses.clause: where control of any sale process relating to those Securities may be lost
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The financing prohibition is qualified, so a facility in which the bank has no independent power of sale (for example, cash-settled legs, a non-recourse structure with no enforcement right over the shares, or security requiring the executive to direct any sale) may fall outside 3.45(b) even though a conventional margin loan does not.

bespoke_clauses.topic: set off and withholding rights are encumbrances
bespoke_clauses.clause: including a mortgage, charge, pledge, lien or title retention arrangement, right of set off or right to withhold payment of a deposit or other money, or any third party interest such as a trust or an equity
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Ordinary bank documentation terms such as set-off and the right to withhold a cash collateral deposit are themselves prohibited encumbrances, so even a lightly secured collar loan is caught.

bespoke_clauses.clause: may be given clearance to Deal as outlined in paragraphs 3.44 and 3.46, except in relation to Securities that are unvested
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unvested plan securities can never be hedged, pledged or dealt with, even in severe financial hardship, so the collateral and hedge pool is limited to vested, unrestricted shares.

bespoke_clauses.clause: this paragraph does not permit the Nominated Qantas Employee to otherwise Deal in those Restricted Securities
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Shares that have vested but remain subject to plan restrictions are also outside the collar pool.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The approval is valid for one month unless another period is agreed by the Chairman or CEO.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any exceptional-circumstances clearance gives a generous one-month execution window compared with the two to five business days common elsewhere, which would comfortably accommodate collar documentation and pricing if such a clearance could be obtained.

bespoke_clauses.clause: “Securities” means shares, options or other securities or derivatives (including any structured financial product, swap, futures contract, contract for difference, spread bet, warrant or depository receipt) issued by any listed entity or issued or created over the listed entity's securities by third parties.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Bank-written OTC options over Qantas shares are Securities with no venue limitation, so entering the collar is a Dealing in its own right and not merely a hedge.

bespoke_clauses.clause: any family member or associate over whom they have influence, including specifically any person who lives in the same home as the Nominated Qantas Employee
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Booking the collar or the loan through a spouse, household member or influenced entity does not escape the paragraph 3.44 and 3.45 restrictions.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Nominated Qantas Employees means Directors, Company Secretaries, Executive Management Members, direct reports to Executive Management Members, and other Executives specifically notified by the CEO or his nominee from time to time.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Employees below direct reports to Executive Management Members are outside the hedging, margin lending and encumbrance prohibitions entirely and face only the statutory insider trading rule, but they are also unlikely to be the bank's target clients.

This is the version lodged under Listing Rule 12.10 in September 2013; a current version should be obtained from the Company Secretary before relying on the analysis, as the hedging and financing paragraphs may have changed.

summary: A funded collar is not available to a director or senior executive of Qantas under this Code. Nominated Qantas Employees (directors, company secretaries, direct reports to the CEO and their direct reports, and anyone else the CEO nominates) have their Dealing definition extended by paragraph 3.45 to catch both legs of the structure: hedging or any contract entered into to secure a profit or avoid a loss by reference to the Qantas share price, and any margin lending, securities lending or grant of charge, lien, pledge, right of set off or third party interest over Qantas Securities where control of the sale process may be lost. Both limbs are unqualified as to vesting state, apply equally to influenced family members and household associates, and there is no clearance path expressed for them; the only relief, paragraph 3.48, is granted by the Chairman or CEO in exceptional circumstances such as severe hardship or a court order, is valid for one month, cannot touch unvested Securities and on its face releases only the paragraph 3.44 prohibition rather than 3.45. Two features are worth testing with the Company Secretary: the drafting of 3.45 is ambiguous between an outright ban and an enlargement of Dealing that would make both legs available with a written Request to Deal outside the 30 June and 31 December Closed Periods, and the financing limb is qualified by 'where control of any sale process relating to those Securities may be lost', which a structure giving the bank no independent power of sale may not trigger. There is no short-term dealing rule, no minimum shareholding requirement and no financier disclosure obligation, so tenor and reporting are not obstacles; ordinary Qantas Employees below the Nominated tier are subject only to the statutory insider trading prohibition.
